name: Battle of Marathon

phases.title: The two armies form their lines
phases.text: The two tribes in the Greek centre were drawn up four ranks deep and the tribes on their flanks eight deep. One explanation is that this made the Athenian line as long as the Persian line.

phases.title: The Greeks advance and the lines meet
phases.text: On a signal from Miltiades the Athenians advanced and probably broke into a run at the limit of the archers' effectiveness. They went through the Persian arrows, protected for the most part by their armour, and met the enemy line.

phases.title: The Greek centre is pushed back
phases.text: The fighting lasted a long time. In the centre the Persians and Sacae prevailed and broke through in pursuit inland, while on each wing the Athenians and Plataeans prevailed.

phases.title: The Persian wings are routed
phases.text: The Athenian and Plataean wings quickly routed the Persian levies on the flanks, which were of poorer quality than the troops in the centre.

phases.title: The Greek wings turn inwards on the centre
phases.text: The Athenian wings then turned inwards to surround the Persian centre, which had been more successful against the thin Greek centre.

phases.title: The Persian centre breaks and flees to the ships
phases.text: The Persian centre broke in panic towards its ships, pursued by the Greeks. Some, unaware of the local terrain, ran towards the swamps, where unknown numbers drowned.

note: The accounts give no compass directions, so the sides are drawn with the Athenians at the top and the sea at the bottom, and wings are named by their place on the plan. The accounts do not say on which wing the Plataeans stood, or where the line lay in relation to the camp; Mount Agrieliki and the swamps are placed on the sides the story needs. The Persian cavalry is not drawn. The accounts do not say where the Persian wings fled.
